newsitem.title: USA: Three Cubans on trial in Florida for air piracy.
newsitem.headline: Three Cubans on trial in Florida for air piracy.

text.p: Three Cubans went on trial in U.S. federal court on Monday on charges of air piracy for allegedly hijacking a Cuban plane to Florida last year.
The defendants, Adel Regalado Ulloa, Leonardo Reyes Ramirez and Jose Roberto Bello Puente, all of Havana, could be sentenced to a minimum of 20 years in prison if convicted.
According to federal prosecutors, the trio took control of a Cuban Aero Taxi Service aircraft on Aug 16, 1996 during a scheduled domestic flight and forced the pilot to fly to Florida.
The plane crashed in the Gulf of Mexico near Fort Myers, Florida. The pilot and three passengers were rescued by a Russian freighter and turned over to the U.S. Coast Guard.
At the time, the alleged hijackers asked for asylum and the pilot said he wanted to go home. He was sent home about a week after the skyjacking.
The defendants claim the pilot was a willing participant in the flight to Florida, lawyers for the three said.
Anti-Castro demonstrators rallied in front of the U.S. courthouse in Tampa in support of the defendants at the opening of the trial, which was expected to take about two weeks.
